title: Terraform VPC Stitcher: subnet profiles, NAT HA & endpoint reconciler
creator: Mei Chen
description:
Problem: Private deployments need a production-ready Terraform module that can (1) express subnet profiles (control-plane, gpu/compute, infra), (2) support high-availability NAT/IGW patterns with safe canary upgrades, and (3) reconcile VPC endpoints + route tables to avoid drift during rolling upgrades.

Goal: Deliver a 'vpc-stitcher' Terraform module (v2) and accompanying upgrade/reconciliation pattern that operators can use for new Private VPCs and for rolling upgrades of existing stacks without traffic blips. Module will include: subnet profile schema, nat/igw HA primitives, endpoint attachment abstraction, route-table stitching, and hooks for synthetic health checks and safe rollbacks.

Scope: module code + provider pinning + comprehensive examples + automated plan/apply guard in CI + a lightweight TF-runner workflow (docs + example GitHub Actions) and a canary upgrade playbook. Not in scope: full operator implementation (separate follow-up task), cross-account peering orchestration (handled by other modules).

Design decisions / trade-offs: 
- Approach A (Terraform-only): implement idempotent resources and reconciliation through careful lifecycle/meta-arguments and CR-based automation that runs terraform apply in CI. Pros: familiar to infra teams. Cons: slow upgrades and potential apply contention.
- Approach B (Terraform + Reconciler): keep Terraform for initial provisioning but publish reconciliation hooks (health-check lambda + TF plan-runner) to perform safe in-place upgrades. Pros: faster, allows synthetic checks pre/post. Cons: extra operational surface and auth complexity.

Decision: implement Approach B as default for Private until we have a cluster operator. Provide a thin TF-runner GitHub Action that executes plan -> health-check canary -> apply, with option to fall back to manual apply.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Module exposes subnet profiles and sample mapping for three AZs (control, compute-gpu, infra).
- NAT/IGW configuration supports dual NAT (active/standby) pattern and canary attach/detach flow with zero-downtime for egress.
- Endpoint reconciler ensures S3/Dynamo/SecretsManager endpoints are present and route tables updated during upgrades; terraform plan shows no drift after reconciler run.
- CI action implements canary apply to a tagged test VPC and runs synthetic health probes (HTTP + TCP + route validation) before global apply.
- Automated tests (unit TFLint, terratest integration on ephemeral account) pass in CI.
- Documentation and rollout runbook published in Drive and linked in the ticket.

Implementation notes: 
- Provider pinning: aws provider ~> 5.0 with explicit feature flags.
- Use resource tagging and naming conventions to enable safe lookup and drift detection.
- Route table stitching uses explicit aws_route_table_association resources (avoid reliance on default behavior).
- NAT HA uses two NAT Gateways with a failover route-table swap pattern implemented in TF-runner via a short-lived network change with health checks.

Risks: 
- IAM complexity for TF-runner and health check lambdas (mitigation: scoped roles + ephemeral tokens).
- Quota/limits when running terratest in CI (mitigation: shared sandbox pool with quota guard).

Docs & artifacts: see links field for spec, example code and PRs.
acceptance_criteria: Subnet profile schema documented + example mapping for 3 AZs
Dual NAT HA pattern implemented with canary attach/detach flow
Endpoint reconciler prevents plan drift for S3/Dynamo/SecretsManager endpoints
CI GitHub Action for canary-plan -> health-check -> apply exists
Terratest integration covers create/upgrade/destroy happy path
